summary: Union County, TN tower built by the CCC around 1935 for the TVA; state-owned since 1952; NRHP-listed 2021; standing in Chuck Swan State Forest.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 type; 100-foot galvanized steel tower with an observation cab

staffing.status: state stopped using its fire towers on a continuous basis around 1971

facts.agency: Tennessee Division of Forestry; built by the CCC for the Tennessee Valley Authority, which sold it to the state in 1952

events.note: Built ca. 1935 by the Civilian Conservation Corps for the TVA (nomination). The National Register multiple property form and Wikidata give 1934
TVA sold the tower and surrounding forest land to the State of Tennessee; the state renamed the site for Commissioner Charles 'Chuck' Swan, who oversaw the purchase
Period of significance ends in 1971, about when the state ceased to use its fire towers on a continuous basis (statewide statement in nomination)
Radio tower and equipment building added nearby (nomination: ca. 2013; aerial images place construction between April 2012 and November 2013)
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places on June 28, 2021

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Nomination says ca. 1935; the multiple property form and Wikidata say 1934. The story reports the disagreement and uses the nomination's ca. 1935.
Nomination gives 1,663 feet in one place and 1,660 feet in another; Tennessee Landforms lists 1674 feet. Elevation is not used in the story.

corrections.proposed: Tennessee Division of Forestry (state-owned since 1952; built by the CCC for the TVA)
corrections.why: TVA sold the tower and its land to the State of Tennessee in 1952, and the nomination says the Division of Forestry now manages it. TVA was the original owner.

notes_for_editor: Construction year is the main conflict (1934 vs ca. 1935). No public access rules were found, so no access key is recorded; the story says the sources do not say whether the public may visit. The Forest Lookouts page for this tower gives only the agency (TVA) and county, with no year. The Chuck Swan State Forest page was not checked. Staffing as_of uses the nomination's 1971 end date for continuous use.
